 I.   BACKGROUND & APPLICABILITY
      This bulletin provides guidance to owners and contractors regarding the reopening of sites whose
      operations were suspended pursuant to New York State Gubernatorial Emergency Order 202.6
      and subsequent orders and related Empire State Development Corporation guidelines, New York
      City Mayoral Emergency Order 103 and subsequent mayoral emergency orders, or as otherwise
      warranted due to the ongoing COVID-19 public health emergency.


 II. HEALTH PRECAUTIONS
      All applicable guidance from local, state, and federal health officials must be followed.


 III. RESUMPTION OF OPERATIONS
      As construction and demolition sites resume operations under "Phase 1" and subsequent
      reopening phases, the following measures shall apply:
      - Until operations resume, continue to follow the requirements of Buildings Bulletin 2020-006,
        or subsequent bulletins.
      - Once operations resume, follow all requirements of Chapter 33 of the Building Code and
        related rules, and other applicable laws, in order to safeguard the site.

      - If your site resumes operations, but subsequently must suspend operations again due to the
        ongoing COVID-19 public health emergency:

           - Notify the Department upon the suspension of operations.
           - Follow the requirements of Buildings Bulletin 2020-006, or subsequent bulletins, until
             operations resume.
           - If operations do not resume within three months of the subsequent suspension, the site
             will be considered to be ?interrupted or abandoned and discontinued? under the provisions
             of Section 3303.13 of the Building Code.


  IV. REQUIREMENTS FOR SITES THAT REMAIN SUSPENDED
       The following provisions shall apply to sites that remain suspended and do not resume
       construction operations:
       -   Until operations resume, continue to follow the requirements of Buildings Bulletin 2020-006,
           or subsequent bulletins.
       -   Once operations resume, follow all requirements of Chapter 33 of the Building Code and
           related rules, and other applicable laws, in order to safeguard the site.
       -   If operations do not resume within three months of the suspension, the site will be considered
           to be ?interrupted or abandoned and discontinued? under the provisions of Section 3303.13 of
           the Building Code.


  V. REQUIREMENTS FOR SITES THAT ARE ?INTERRUPTED OR ABANDONED
     AND DISCONTINUED"
      All provisions shall apply to sites that are ?interrupted or abandoned and discontinued?under
      Section 3303.13 of the Building Code, including but not limited to the following:
      - The site must be secured with a fence in accordance with Section 3303.13.1 of the Building
        Code.
      - A safety monitoring plan for the site shall be prepared and submitted to the department in
        accordance with Section 3303.13.2 of the Building Code. The monitoring plan shall cover all
        applicable items in Sections III, IV, and V of Buildings Bulletin 2020-006, or subsequent
        bulletins, as well as all applicable items in Section 3303.13.2 of the Building Code.
      - The site shall be monitored in accordance with the safety monitoring plan.
      - Inspections of sites that are ?interrupted or abandoned and discontinued? shall be performed
        at least monthly.
      - Submittal of inspection reports to the department for sites that are ?interrupted or abandoned
        and discontinued? shall occur at least monthly.
      - Sites shall be filled and graded or otherwise secured in accordance with Section 3303.13.3 of
        the Building Code.
